methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two information sources.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Detect falling edge on each bit of a 32-bit input vector
Circuit has a synchronous active-high reset input
Output bit is set to 1 when a falling edge is detected on the corresponding input bit
Output bit remains 1 until the reset signal is asserted
Output register is initialized to 0 when reset is asserted
spec_atomic_units: Module has a 32-bit input `in`
Module has a clock input `clk`
Module has a reset input `reset`
Module has a 32-bit output `out`
`reset` signal is active high and synchronous
`clk` signal synchronizes the operation
Function is to capture falling edges on a bit-by-bit basis of the input `in`
Output `out` held high until reset is asserted
Input sampled at each clock cycle
Previous value of `in` stored in internal register (in_delayed)
Falling edge detected when `in_delayed[i]` is 1 and `in[i]` is 0
Output `out[i]` is set to 1 when a falling edge is detected on the corresponding input bit `in[i]`
Output remains at 1 until the `reset` signal is asserted
If `reset` is asserted (high), `out[i]` is set to 0
If `reset` is not asserted and `falling_edge[i]` is true, `out[i]` is set to 1
If `reset` is not asserted and `falling_edge[i]` is false, `out[i]` retains its previous value
Register (in_delayed) stores the previous value of the input `in`
Combinational block detects the falling edge for each bit
Register (out) stores the output value for each bit
Output register is updated based on the reset signal and the falling edge detection logic
Falling edge detection logic: falling_edge[i] = in_delayed[i] AND NOT(in[i])
Output Logic: out[i] = (reset) ? 0 : ((falling_edge[i]) ? 1 : out[i]_previous)
NOT Gate used to generate NOT(in[i])
AND Gate combines in_delayed[i] and NOT(in[i]) to produce falling_edge[i]
Multiplexer selects the value for out[i] based on reset and falling_edge[i]
Output `out` is updated synchronously with the rising edge of `clk`
The `reset` signal resets the output `out` to 0 on the next rising edge of `clk`
Falling edge detection is also synchronous to `clk`
The design uses registers: `out` and `in_prev`
Non-blocking assignments (`<=`) are used to update both `out` and `in_prev`
The falling edge detection logic compares the current value of `in` with the previous value stored in `in_prev`
The reset is synchronous and active high
